evidence.text: The entry favors an account in which early Western Zhou inscriptions used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic marker distinguished 考, with the lower 匕 of 老 usually omitted. The entry says early bronze 丂 used for ‘father’ lends that account support, but judges the 老-based account better able to explain early Western Zhou usage. These are attributed analyses, not settled formation history.
